title: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
objectives: Understand FCM via a real-life analogy
Send + receive notification vs data messages on Android/iOS/Web
Manage tokens, topics, and segmented delivery
Handle foreground / background / terminated state correctly
Beat Android Doze / iOS BG restrictions

sections.markdown:
**Think of FCM as the postal service for your app.**

Every device carries a **PO Box number** (the FCM registration token). Your server writes letters (messages) and hands them to the FCM post office. The post office looks up the PO Box (or a **topic** — a public mailbox everyone can subscribe to), and delivers.

Two very different types of mail:

- **Notification message** — a POSTCARD with a title + body already printed. The post office (Android/iOS system) shows it on the door mat (notification tray) even if you're not home. When you come home + tap it, your app opens. Great for user-visible reminders.
- **Data message** — a SEALED ENVELOPE with structured JSON. The post office wakes your app briefly to open it. Your app decides what to do — schedule a background sync, update a badge, refresh a widget. NEVER shown by the system.

**The catch — governments regulate the postal service.** Android Doze/App Standby, iOS Low-Data-Mode + battery drain protection all *delay or drop* letters when the phone thinks the app doesn't matter. High-priority envelopes get through; low-priority queue up. **Data messages are LESS reliable than notification messages for wakeups** — never use them for critical alerts.

**PO Box numbers change.** Reinstalls, factory resets, restore-from-backup all issue a new token. Your server MUST refresh + de-dup or send to dead boxes. Store `(user_id, token)` pairs; rotate on `onTokenRefresh`.

**Why every consumer mobile app has this on day one:** re-engagement drives retention. Chats, order updates, delivery tracking, marketing campaigns, background sync — nearly every notification on your phone leaves a Firebase-linked server via FCM.

**Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)** is a cross-platform push messaging service for Android, iOS, Web, Flutter, Unity. Server sends a message via **HTTP v1 API** (OAuth-signed) to a **token**, a **topic** (fan-out to all subscribers), a **condition** (topic AND/OR), or a **device group** (deprecated). FCM handles delivery to Google Play Services (Android), APNs (iOS), Web Push (browsers). Free at any volume. Two message types: **notification** (system-tray, auto-displayed) and **data** (JSON to your handler, silent). Both can carry either payload.

## Server-side HTTP v1 (Node.js Admin SDK)
## Common mistakes

**Mistake 1: Treating token as durable identity.** Tokens rotate on reinstall, factory reset, app clear, SDK upgrade. Store `(user_id, token, updated_at)`; refresh on `onTokenRefresh`; delete rows Fcm reports as `UNREGISTERED`.

**Mistake 2: Data messages for critical delivery.** Android Doze delays them for hours; iOS drops silent ones when the app is terminated (unless `content-available: 1` + APNs cooperation). Use notification messages for user-visible; data for opportunistic sync.
**Mistake 3: Background handler NOT top-level.** Must be `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` + top-level function. Otherwise Dart isolate can't find the entrypoint → the handler never runs on Android.
**Mistake 4: Forgetting Firebase.initializeApp() in bg handler.** Runs in a fresh isolate; must re-init to touch Firestore, Analytics, etc.
**Mistake 5: iOS APNs setup missing.** No APNs key uploaded → iOS delivers nothing. Requires an APNs Auth Key or Certificate + Push Notifications capability + entitlements.
**Mistake 6: Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission not requested.** Silent-fail default. Request via `requestPermission`.
**Mistake 7: One channel for all.** Android channels group notifications; users can mute per-channel. Create `orders`, `promotions`, `chat` channels + let users control.
**Mistake 8: Legacy server-key auth.** Deprecated since June 2024. Move to HTTP v1 API (OAuth-signed) or Firebase Admin SDK.
**Mistake 9: No de-duplication.** Same push retried → duplicate notifications. Use `collapseKey` (Android) / `apns-collapse-id` (iOS).
**Mistake 10: Not respecting quiet hours + region.** Sending 3 AM local time = uninstall. Track user timezone; batch to daytime windows.
## Best practices
**1. Register tokens by (user_id, token) + refresh on onTokenRefresh + delete UNREGISTERED tokens.**
**2. Notification for user-visible; data for silent sync.** Never mix critical delivery in data-only.
**3. Wire flutter_local_notifications for foreground display + rich content.**
**4. Android notification channels** — create per-category; users can mute selectively.
**5. High priority + collapse keys** — deduplicate + wake for real deliveries.
**6. Topics for mass segments** (news, sports); server-token targeting for personal messages.
**7. Deep linking via `data.deep_link`** — parse in `onMessageOpenedApp` + `getInitialMessage`.
**8. Guarantee background work via WorkManager / BGTasks** — data message triggers, not the source of truth.
**9. HTTP v1 API only; sign requests via OAuth (Admin SDK does this).**
**10. Send in local business hours + honor per-user preferences.**
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy) — Foreground notification.** Wire onMessage; log payload; display via flutter_local_notifications.
**Practice 2 (Medium) — Background data.** Set up top-level onBackgroundMessage; verify isolate wakes + writes to Hive on Android.
**Practice 3 (Medium) — Topics.** Subscribe to `promo_india`; server sends to topic; verify all subscribers receive.
**Practice 4 (Hard) — Token management.** (user_id, token) table in your backend + rotate on onTokenRefresh + purge UNREGISTERED tokens on send failure.
**Practice 5 (Hard) — Deep linking.** Data payload `deep_link=/orders/123`; parse in onMessageOpenedApp + getInitialMessage; navigate correctly.
**Practice 6 (Expert) — Guaranteed background sync.** Data message → WorkManager job → syncs outbox with backoff; test airplane-mode + Doze scenarios.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What's the difference between notification and data messages, and when do you use each?**

**A:** **Notification messages** carry `notification: {title, body}` and are **auto-displayed by the OS** in the system tray. Foreground listener still fires (via `onMessage`) for tracking, but the OS handles rendering when the app is in background/terminated. **Data messages** carry `data: {...}` — arbitrary key-value JSON — and are **silent to the user**; your app's handler (`onBackgroundMessage` in a separate isolate on Flutter) processes them and decides what to do. **Use notification** for chat, order updates, marketing, delivery — anything the user should see. **Use data** for opportunistic silent tasks: bump a badge count, invalidate a cache, trigger a WorkManager sync. **Reliability differs sharply:** notification messages are delivered by the system (high priority in Doze); data messages **on iOS** require `content-available: 1` + APNs cooperation and can be dropped when the app is terminated; **on Android** they're delayed under Doze/App Standby unless flagged high priority. **A single message can carry BOTH payloads** — the notification renders, and if the user opens the app, `data` is available.

**Q2: How do tokens work and when do they rotate?**

**A:** On first FCM init, the SDK calls Google (Android) or APNs (iOS) and receives an opaque **registration token** unique to (device × app × Firebase project × SDK-instance). It's what your server addresses to reach that installation. **Rotation happens on:** reinstall, factory reset, cleared app data, restore-from-backup to a new device, `deleteToken`, Google Play Services updates, SDK upgrades. Not deterministic — could happen anytime. **Handle:** subscribe to `onTokenRefresh` stream; POST every new token to your server with the user_id; store `(user_id, token, last_seen_at)` rows. **On send failure with error `UNREGISTERED` or `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, DELETE the row** — token is dead. **One user, many tokens** (Android + iPad + web) — send to all, or use topics. **NEVER treat token as user identity** — always resolve via your `(user_id, token)` mapping. **Failing to prune dead tokens** is the #1 reason for silent delivery-rate degradation over time.

**Q3: How do you get guaranteed background execution when Android Doze / iOS restrictions get in the way?**

**A:** You can't — mobile OSes will always suppress background execution to save battery. **But you can layer for maximum reliability:** **(1) High-priority notification message** — OS shows in tray + wakes the app when user taps. Most reliable path for user-visible tasks. **(2) Data + notification hybrid** — notification renders; if user opens, `data` triggers the sync work. **(3) Data message with `content-available: 1` on iOS** + **high priority on Android** — best-effort silent wake. **(4) OFFLOAD to WorkManager (Android) / BGTaskScheduler (iOS)** — data message ARRIVES → your handler enqueues a WorkManager job with `NetworkType.CONNECTED` + backoff. Job runs when OS allows — could be minutes later, but WILL run. This is the pattern for outbox sync, background upload, offline queues. **(5) Silent-push escalation** — if silent push didn't wake the app after N tries, fall back to visible notification. **(6) Server-side retry** with backoff — FCM auto-retries; also implement app-level retry. **The senior mindset:** treat FCM as a hint that work is needed, WorkManager as the actual executor.

**Q4: Notification vs topic vs condition targeting — what to pick when?**

**A:** **Direct token send** (`send({token})`) — precise, one device. Use for **personalized** messages: order shipped, DM received, per-user reminder. Cost is one API call per device (batched up to 500 via `sendEachForMulticast`). **Topic** (`send({topic: 'sports'})`) — client `subscribeToTopic('sports')`; server fan-outs to all subscribers with ONE call. Perfect for **broadcast segments** (news alerts, promo campaigns). Cost is O(1) server-side. **Condition** (`send({condition: "'sports' in topics && 'india' in topics"})`) — Boolean over up to 5 topics — sports fans in India. **Server-side segments (audiences)** — Firebase Cloud Messaging campaign targeting via Analytics audiences (`plan=pro AND last_purchase < 7d ago`). **Rule of thumb:** personal notifications → tokens; broad campaigns → topics or audiences; complex intersections → conditions. **Not to use:** Legacy 'device group' API (deprecated); homegrown 'topic per user' schemes explode server-side and rate-limit you.

**Q5: How does deep linking from a notification work?**

**A:** Server sends a `data.deep_link` field (e.g., `/orders/123`) alongside notification. Three delivery paths matter: **(1) Foreground** — `onMessage` fires immediately; you decide whether to render (via flutter_local_notifications) or handle in-place. **(2) Background** — OS renders notification; user taps → app resumes → `onMessageOpenedApp` stream emits with the RemoteMessage → parse `deep_link` + navigate. **(3) Terminated** — OS renders + tap → app cold-starts → `getInitialMessage()` returns the tap-launched RemoteMessage → parse + navigate (BEFORE removing splash). **Router hookup:** GoRouter / Navigator 2.0's `go(deep_link)`. **Gotchas:** (a) Auth state may not be loaded yet when `getInitialMessage` fires — buffer until sign-in resolves. (b) Some Android launchers strip data; test on real devices. (c) Universal links / App Links can replace this pattern for HTTPS deep-links — often simpler.

**Q6: What migration steps did the legacy server-key deprecation force?**

**A:** In **June 2024** Google deprecated the **legacy HTTP + XMPP FCM APIs** (the ones that used the static `AAAA...` server key from console → HTTP Authorization header). **Replaced by:** **HTTP v1 API** — signed by **OAuth 2.0 access tokens** obtained from a **service-account key** (from Google Cloud IAM). **Migration path:** (1) Rotate to service-account JSON key; store in Secret Manager / KMS. (2) On the server, `admin.initializeApp()` (Node) or use Google Auth libs to sign requests. (3) Move payload shape from `{ to, notification, data }` to `{ message: { token, notification, android, apns, webpush, data } }` — nested platform-specific overrides. (4) Update batch endpoints to `sendEachForMulticast`. (5) Rotate keys periodically. **Why the change:** static server keys were long-lived credentials; a leaked key = full FCM abuse to your project. OAuth tokens are short-lived + can be scoped + audited. Every serious app had to migrate; interviewers know this + look for it.

## Real-world usage

- **Chat apps** (WhatsApp-style) — new message → data + notification hybrid.
- **E-commerce** — order placed / shipped / delivered.
- **Delivery apps** — driver location updates + arrival ETA.
- **Content apps** — breaking news via topics.
- **Marketing** — segment campaigns via Analytics audiences.
- **Silent sync** — data messages trigger WorkManager to fetch fresh feed.
- **Web push** — desktop reminders in browsers.

## Advanced notes

- **Rich notifications** — images, action buttons: `notification.image` field + native BigPicture / NotificationServiceExtension.
- **Notification service extension (iOS)** — modify payload before display (decrypt, download image).
- **Notification channels (Android 8+)** — per-category importance + user mute; required for O+.
- **Priority + collapse keys** — `high` priority for urgent, `normal` for opportunistic; `collapse_key` merges rapid retries.
- **APNs entitlements + Push Notifications capability** — Xcode capability + provisioning profile must include push.
- **Web Push** — VAPID keys + service worker; delivery uses the browser's push service.
- **Interruption levels (iOS 15+)** — passive/active/time-sensitive/critical.
- **Delivery diagnostics** — Firebase console shows delivery per-device via FCM Delivery.
- **`sendAll` / `sendEachForMulticast`** — up to 500 tokens per batch call.
- **BigQuery integration** — Cloud Messaging export logs delivery events.
- **In-app messaging** — Firebase IAM is a complement — targeted pop-ups WHILE the app is open.
- **FCM + iOS Live Activities** — special APNs payloads for lockscreen widgets.
- **Delegated sending** — Cloud Function trigger on Firestore write publishes a message.

flashcards.back: Notification = auto-displayed by OS; data = silent, handler decides.
Top-level function, @pragma('vm:entry-point'), Firebase.initializeApp() inside — runs in a separate isolate.
Reinstall, factory reset, cleared data, restore-from-backup, SDK upgrade. Subscribe onTokenRefresh.
OAuth access token from service-account key (Admin SDK signs automatically). Legacy server key is deprecated.
Data message → WorkManager (Android) / BGTaskScheduler (iOS). FCM alone can't guarantee execution.
